description: Eval set for PRD 8.1, retrieval quality. 25 role-and-level query fixtures drawn from seed/questions/*.json, the exact files the seeded bank was built from. Relevant sets are model-judged (by the Test Author subagent reading every seed question directly), standing in for the PRD's human-judged relevant sets; flagged for a spot check before this suite is treated as a durable ground truth. Ids are resolved from text at run time by evals/suites/retrieval.ts since ids differ per environment. None of the 5 deliberately non-compliant questions in seed/known-flagged.json are referenced here.

fixtures.name: engineering_junior_growth_signal
fixtures.context: First engineering hire fresh out of a bootcamp; want signal on learning velocity, humility under correction, and communication under uncertainty, not deep systems experience.
relevant: How do you decide when code needs a comment?
Describe a time you had to learn a new language or framework under deadline. How did you approach it?
Tell me about a time a senior engineer disagreed with your approach and turned out to be wrong. How did you handle it?
What is your approach when you estimate a task at two days and on day three it is still not done?
Why engineering, and why now at this kind of company?

fixtures.name: engineering_mid_debugging_and_legacy_code
fixtures.context: Backend-heavy mid-level engineer; want debugging rigor, testing discipline, and handling legacy code, not general team-culture chat.
relevant: Tell me about a bug that took you days to find. How did you finally track it down?
Describe a time you had to make a tradeoff between shipping quickly and doing it right. What did you choose and why?
Tell me about a time you inherited someone else's code that you found difficult. What did you do?
How do you approach writing tests? What do you test first and what do you skip?
How would you explain a race condition to a non-technical stakeholder whose feature is delayed by one?
How do you keep a pull request reviewable? What is your personal size or scope limit?
What would you do in your first month to become productive in a codebase of two hundred thousand lines?

fixtures.name: engineering_senior_production_ownership
fixtures.context: Senior backend engineer for a systems-heavy team; want evidence of production ownership, technical judgment under pressure, and system design depth, not general career motivation.
relevant: Walk me through the most technically complex system you have built or significantly changed. What made it hard, and what did you personally contribute?
Describe a production incident you were involved in. What was your role during and after?
Walk me through how you would design a rate limiter for a public API.
Tell me about a technical decision you made that you later reversed. What triggered the reversal?
Describe a system you monitored in production. What signals did you watch and which one saved you at least once?
Walk me through how you profile and fix a slow endpoint.

fixtures.name: product_management_mid_hypothesis_driven_discovery
fixtures.context: Mid-level PM candidate for a fast-moving startup; want hypothesis-driven discovery, decision hygiene, and a healthy engineering partnership, not a single motivational answer.
relevant: Tell me about a product decision you made with incomplete data. How did you decide, and what happened?
Walk me through how you validated a feature idea before building it. What did you do when the evidence was mixed?
Tell me about a time engineering told you something was impossible in the timeframe. What did you do?
Describe how you ran your most recent user research. Who did you talk to, and what changed as a result?
How do you write a good problem statement? Walk me through one you wrote recently.
How do you keep engineers connected to the why behind the roadmap? Give an example.
How do you document decisions so the team does not relitigate them in three months?

fixtures.name: product_management_senior_high_stakes_stakeholders
fixtures.context: Senior PM handling high-stakes external stakeholders, enterprise customers and competitive pressure; want conviction and communication under pressure from real scenario-based stories.
relevant: Describe a feature you killed. How did you make the call and communicate it?
Tell me about a time you had to say no to an important customer. How did you do it?
Tell me about the hardest stakeholder you have managed. What made it hard and what worked?
Tell me about a time you changed your roadmap because of a competitor's move. Or chose not to. Why?
Tell me about a B2B deal that pressured you to build something off-roadmap. What did you do?

fixtures.name: product_management_lead_scope_and_leadership
fixtures.context: Group PM or Lead PM opening; want lead-level judgment across people development, cross-team alignment, political navigation, and commercial thinking.
relevant: Walk me through a pricing or packaging decision you were part of. What data informed it?
As a group PM or lead, how do you develop the PMs under you? Give a specific example of someone you grew.
Tell me about a time you aligned three or more teams behind one goal. What almost derailed it?
Walk me through how you would decide between two features when each has a vocal executive sponsor.

fixtures.name: sales_junior_prospecting_and_hygiene
fixtures.context: Entry-level SDR or AE hire; want prospecting method, operational hygiene, and resilience, not abstract motivation framing.
relevant: Describe your approach to prospecting. What does your first outreach to a cold account actually look like?
How do you use your CRM? What do you log religiously and what do you skip?
How do you learn a new product well enough to sell it credibly? How long does that take you?
Describe your relationship with rejection. What is your actual recovery routine after a brutal no?

fixtures.name: sales_deal_specific_storytelling
fixtures.context: General sales screen across levels; want deal-specific storytelling: recovery from a lost deal, walking away from a bad deal, and pattern recognition across lost deals, not general team-culture chat.
relevant: Tell me about a deal you lost that you should have won. What did you learn?
How do you qualify out of a deal? Tell me about a time you walked away.
Tell me about a deal where the champion left the company mid-cycle. What did you do?
Describe a time you disagreed with your sales manager about deal strategy. What happened?
Tell me about a time you spotted a pattern across lost deals and changed something systemic.

fixtures.name: customer_success_mid_proactive_account_management
fixtures.context: Mid-level CSM at a B2B SaaS company managing a portfolio of accounts; want proactive account management, expansion instinct with trust preserved, and honest expectation-setting, not general culture-fit stories.
relevant: Tell me about a customer you saved from churning. What was your read on the real reason they were leaving?
How do you run a quarterly business review that executives actually attend? What is on your agenda?
Walk me through your onboarding playbook for a new account. Where do accounts most often stall?
Tell me about a time a customer demanded a feature you knew was not coming. How did you handle it?
How do you prioritize a book of forty accounts? Which ones get your proactive time?
Tell me about a time you delivered bad news to a customer: an outage, a deprecation, a price change. How did you frame it?
What is your approach in the first call with an account that has been ignored for six months?
Tell me about a time you said no to a customer request and kept the relationship strong.

fixtures.name: customer_success_lead_track_portfolio_scope
fixtures.context: Customer success team lead search; want scenario-based role stories showing account ownership at increasing scope, from single-account saves to portfolio-level pattern recognition, appropriate for a lead-track hire.
relevant: Describe a customer you could not save. Looking back, when was the save actually lost?
Tell me about your most demanding customer ever. How did you keep the relationship healthy?
How do you turn a frustrated power user into a champion? Give a real example.
Describe a time you noticed a pattern across several accounts and pushed a systemic fix.
Tell me about a renewal negotiation where the customer had real leverage. How did it resolve?
How would you rebuild trust after our own product caused a customer's worst week of the quarter?
Tell me about a customer you saved from churning. What was your read on the real reason they were leaving?

fixtures.name: data_analytics_junior_rigor_habits
fixtures.context: Junior data analyst hire; want rigor habits, SQL hygiene and reproducibility, over motivational framing.
relevant: Walk me through your SQL habits. What does your query look like just before you share results?
What kind of analytical problem makes you lose track of time?
How do you document your analyses so someone can reproduce them in six months?
What analytics work do you find tedious, and how do you make yourself do it well anyway?

fixtures.name: data_analytics_mid_technical_method_only
fixtures.context: Mid-level analyst; deep dive on technical and analytical method: data validation, statistical communication, diagnostic investigation, cohort analysis. Skill-only screen, no culture or motivation questions.
relevant: Describe your approach to validating a dataset you have never seen before.
How do you explain confidence intervals to a stakeholder who just wants the number?
Walk me through how you would investigate a sudden 20 percent drop in a key metric.
Walk me through a time you used cohort analysis to answer a retention question. What did you find?

fixtures.name: data_analytics_senior_judgment_under_scrutiny
fixtures.context: Senior analyst for a data team with real executive visibility; want judgment under scrutiny: error ownership, executive communication, and high-stakes verification, not tooling-evaluation experience.
relevant: Tell me about a time your analysis was wrong and someone acted on it. What happened next?
Tell me about a metric you built that the company still uses. Why did it stick?
Tell me about presenting analysis to executives. What did you cut from the deck, and why?
Describe a time you had to tell a leader their favorite metric was misleading.
What is the difference between an insight and an observation? Give me one of each from your last role.
Tell me about a data quality issue you caught just before it went to the board or an investor.

fixtures.name: design_mid_craft_process_end_to_end
fixtures.context: Mid-level product designer; want craft process end to end: concept evolution, accessibility habit, handoff discipline, and prototyping and iteration, not interpersonal collaboration-style stories.
relevant: Walk me through a design in your portfolio where the final version differs sharply from your first concept. What changed it?
Describe your handoff process to engineers. What do you include that prevents the most rework?
Walk me through how you approach accessibility in your work. Give a specific decision from a recent project.
Describe designing something under a deadline that did not allow research. What did you do instead?
Tell me about designing for mobile and desktop simultaneously. What broke and how did you resolve it?
How do you know when a design is done enough to ship?
Describe a time you tested a prototype with real users. What did you change based on round one?

fixtures.name: design_lead_track_design_leadership
fixtures.context: Design lead opening; want design leadership specifically: delegation discipline, coaching, executive presence, and defending design decisions with data, not general craft-process questions.
relevant: Tell me about a time user research contradicted your design instinct. What did you do?
Describe a time you simplified a flow that had grown complicated. What did you cut and who objected?
What is your relationship with data in design decisions? Tell me about a time metrics and usability conflicted.
How do you present design work to executives? What do you show first?
As a design lead, how do you review work without redesigning it yourself? Give an example.
Tell me about growing a designer who was technically strong but struggled with communication.

fixtures.name: finance_senior_runway_and_forecast_discipline
fixtures.context: Senior FP&A finance hire for a company managing runway carefully; want forecast rigor, cash discipline, integrity under revenue-recognition pressure, and high-stakes ownership.
relevant: Tell me about a forecast you got significantly wrong. What was the miss, and what did you change in your method?
Describe a time you found an error in numbers that had already been reported. What did you do?
Tell me about supporting a fundraise or major financing event. What did you own?
Describe a cost-cutting exercise you ran. How did you decide what was actually cuttable?
Tell me about a time sales or another team pressured you to book something aggressively. What did you do?
Describe your experience with cash flow management in a company watching its runway.
Describe working with auditors. Tell me about a finding you disputed and how it resolved.

fixtures.name: finance_mid_process_craft
fixtures.context: Mid-level FP&A analyst; want concrete process craft: close discipline, systems migration survival, and automation initiative. Skill-only technical screen.
relevant: Describe your month-end close process. Where were the recurring bottlenecks and what did you do about them?
Tell me about implementing or migrating a finance system. What broke, and how did you keep the close on time?
Walk me through variance analysis you performed that uncovered a real operational problem.
Tell me about automating a manual finance process. What did you use and what did it free you to do?

fixtures.name: marketing_mid_measurable_execution
fixtures.context: Mid-level growth or content marketer; want campaign measurement rigor, launch execution discipline, and organic-channel results, not brand philosophy or sales-relationship stories.
relevant: Tell me about the best campaign you have run. Walk me through the numbers from spend to outcome.
Describe a campaign that flopped. What was your hypothesis going in, and where did it break?
Walk me through your approach to a product launch. What is on your checklist that most people forget?
Describe a piece of content that generated pipeline months after publication. What made it durable?
Describe your experience with marketing automation. Tell me about a workflow you built that saved real time.
Walk me through an SEO or organic growth initiative you led. What moved and over what timeline?

fixtures.name: marketing_senior_strategic_judgment
fixtures.context: Senior brand and positioning marketer; want strategic judgment: positioning method, budget allocation discipline, measurement sophistication, and conviction under executive pressure.

How do you decide which channels deserve budget? Tell me about a channel you cut.
How do you measure brand marketing when leadership wants attribution for everything?
Tell me about a rebrand or messaging overhaul you were part of. What almost went wrong?
How do you balance data-driven decisions with creative conviction? Give an example where they conflicted.
Describe your experience with paid acquisition. Walk me through a budget you managed and its efficiency over time.
Tell me about a time marketing and product disagreed about what the product actually is. How did you resolve the story?

fixtures.name: operations_mid_process_and_vendor_rigor
fixtures.context: Mid-level operations generalist; want process-design rigor, vendor and SLA management, and metric discipline, not motivational framing.

fixtures.name: operations_senior_scale_and_triage
